subject: ClevrHealth dedicated capacity blueprint & staggered GPU onramp
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@clevrhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClevrHealth dedicated capacity blueprint & staggered GPU onramp

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a compact dedicated-capacity blueprint that maps to the three usage phases you described (pilot, steady-state, growth). The attached PDF (clevr_dedicated_blueprint_v1.pdf) and burn sheet (projected_burn_sheet_v2.xlsx) show estimated cluster sizing, minimum-GPU commitments, and a staged onboarding cadence. Highlights below: 

- Option Canary (low-risk pilot): 8 A100-sim GPUs (pinned lane), 2-week pilot, auto-burst to shared capacity beyond 80% utilization. Minimum guaranteed GPUs = 8.
- Option Core (recommended for launch): 24 A100-sim GPUs across 2 nodes (12/12), 6-week onboarding window with staggered activation (8 -> 16 -> 24), pre-warmed KV cache for prompt templates. Minimum guaranteed GPUs = 12 during weeks 1–2, 18 weeks 3–4, full 24 at week 5.
- Option Scale (growth posture): 48 GPUs with soft-burst to 64 for traffic spikes, warm pool enabled. Ramp schedule negotiable; suggested 3-month step-up. Minimum guaranteed GPUs = 24 for first 30 days after scale trigger.

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for the 6-week launch to keep latency below 120ms p50 for 1k–2k qps.
- We can set a fallback policy that routes requests to a smaller quantized variant if the dedicated lane reaches 95% sustained utilization.
- Pricing in the appendix is usage + reserved GPU tranche; I included examples for a 12-month commitment vs. 6-month pilot extension.

Next steps I suggest: you confirm which option most closely matches the org appetite (Canary/Core/Scale) and share any internal throughput forecasts (qps, average context length) so we can finalize the activation schedule and SLA targets.

I've cc'd Karthik and Priyom for technical sizing notes — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk the numbers.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: clevr_dedicated_blueprint_v1.pdf (proposal PDF), projected_burn_sheet_v2.xlsx (workbook)
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@clevrhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@clevrhealth.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ClevrHealth dedicated capacity blueprint & staggered GPU onramp

Neha —

Thanks for the clear options and the two attachments. A few clarifying questions before we share internally with the execs: 

1) Minimum guarantee: our procurement team is nervous about a 24 GPU minimum for launch (Core). Can you outline a lower-guarantee variant that still preserves latency SLOs — for example a 16->24 stagger instead of 12->18->24? What would the p95 latency impact look like if we hold the min at 16?

2) Bursting & SLA: you mentioned auto-burst to shared capacity and a fallback to a quantized variant. Is bursting subject to availability (best-effort) or SLA-backed? We need clear language for the SOW about burst cadence and failover behavior.

3) Timeline: we'd prefer a longer pilot runway if possible (6 weeks) — is that something you can offer under the same rate card, or does it require a revised pricing table?

Finally, can we get a quick one-pager focused solely on the activation cadence (what happens week-by-week) for the exec sponsor? Procurement wants the cadence spelled out.

Thanks,
Sofia Martinez
Head of ML Ops, ClevrHealth
sofia.martinez@clevrhealth.com

Subject: Fwd: ClevrHealth dedicated capacity blueprint & staggered GPU onramp (internal notes)

Neha / Priyom —

Forwarding Sofia's questions (below). Quick internal notes so we have a single recommendation before we reply to procurement: 

- Latency vs guarantee: We can support a 16->24 staged minimum (hold 16 guaranteed for first 2 weeks, scale to 20 in week 3, 24 by week 5). With the KV cache warmed and batching set aggressively per prompt families, p95 should remain under 220ms for the 1k qps profile they gave — call that 'Core-lean'. Without cache the p95 climbs to ~420ms under that traffic. I'll attach a compact week-by-week activation one-pager and an alternate burn scenario.

- Bursting: Bursting to shared capacity is best-effort unless they contract a soft-reserve burst window. We can, however, include an SLA-backed burst lane as an add-on (reserved 'burst credits' pool). For SOW clarity, we should phrase the default as 'best-effort burst; documented fallback to quantized model when sustained utilization >95% for 10m'.

- Pricing: extending the pilot to 6 weeks: we can keep the pilot rate but require a short-term extension credit (apply pilot credits to month 1 of a 6mo reserved commit). Simpler to present as '6-week pilot at pilot rate + option to convert credits to reserved commit within 30 days'.

Action items for Neha:
1) Update the Core option to a 'Core-lean' 16->24 path and produce a single-page activation cadence for the exec.
2) Add a small paragraph in the SOW about bursting semantics (best-effort vs add-on SLA).
3) Confirm updated attachments and send to procurement/procurement@clevrhealth.com.

--Karthik

Hi Sofia / procurement team —

Thanks for the prompt questions. Attached is a short update: clevr_dedicated_blueprint_v1.pdf (added a Core-lean 16->24 ramp variant and an explicit week-by-week activation one-pager inside the appendix). Summary of changes: 

- Core-lean: Minimum guarantee sequence = 16 (wk1–2) -> 20 (wk3–4) -> 24 (wk5–6). Expected p95 w/ KV cache & batching: ~200–240ms for 1k qps average request profile.
- Bursting & SLA: Default burst is best-effort to shared pool. We included an optional 'Burst Reserve' add-on (4 GPU credits per month) that can be contractually SLA-backed for predictable overflow. SOW language drafted in the appendix.
- Pilot extension: We can run a 6-week pilot at the pilot rate. If you choose the 6-week path and convert to a 6- or 12-month reserved commit within 30 days, we'll apply the pilot credits against month 1 of the commitment.

Next steps: 
1) If procurement is comfortable with Core-lean, confirm and I will issue an updated commercial summary for signatures (DocuSign).
2) Send any finalized throughput numbers or a short traffic sample (CSV) so we can validate the burn sheet.
3) If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min runbook call (Karthik + Priyom + me) to walk the activation cadence and fallback playbook.

DocuSign & SOW link: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/CLV-2026-089 (placeholder link; final commercial summary will be attached to the DocuSign packet).

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
